texts.preamble: Arvind Goel And 3 Ors vs State Of Assam on 28 May, 2020 Author: Chief Justice Bench: Chief Justice Page No.# 1/5 Gahc010120662012 The Gauhati High Court (High Court Of Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram And Arunachal Pradesh) Case No. : Crl.Pet. 173/2012 1:Arvind Goel and 3 Ors. S/O Sri Mani Ram Goel, 2: Smti Kirti Goel W/O Ari Arvind Goel 3: Sri Abhishek Goel S/O Sri Arvind Goel All Are R/O 2A- Saroj Court Danish Road, Pan Bazar, Ghy-1. 4: Sri Deepak Poddar S/O Sri Pratap Kumar Poddar R/O Swati Apartments Christian Basti, G.S. Road, Ghy Versus 1:State Of Assam Advocate for the Petitioner : Mr.S K Jain Advocate for the Respondent : Before Honourable The Chief Justice Order
texts.facts: 3. Sri Arvind Goel, Smti. Kirti Goel, Sri Abhishek Goel and Sri Deepak Poddar have filed this petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, challenging the proceedings initiated vide C.R. Case No. 2183c/2001, pending in the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Kamrup, Guwahati (transferred to the Court of Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate (II), Sadar, Guwahati). The petitioners have also challenged orders dated 20.02.2002 and 31.10.2011, passed by the Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate (II), Sadar, Guwahati. 4. It appears that a complaint under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short, "Act of 1954") was filed. In course of the proceedings, on 20.02.2002, Summons were issued to summon the accused and the case was fixed for 08.04.2002. On perusal of the order-sheet, it appears that on 08.04.2002 again Summons were ordered to be issued. 5. It appears that two petitions, bearing No. 5781 and 5780 were filed in view of Section 17(4) of the Act of 1954, while taking the plea that the proceedings cannot be initiated against the accused and the prosecution has failed to establish that the offending acts were committed with the consent and connivance of the accused, who happen to be the Directors of M/s Itrik Industries Pvt. Ltd. involved in manufacturing of Bisleri Mineral Water. 6. Order dated 31.10.2011, which is also under challenge, reads as under: "Accuseds are absent with steps. Petitions 5781 & 5780 are allowed. The ld. Counsel for the accused submitted that in view of Section 17(4), the case cannot proceed against the accuseds as the prosecution has failed to established that the act was committed with the consent or connivance of the accuseds. Perused the materials and record. It appears that the complaint has been filed against all the Directors, the company and its production managers alleging that they were responsible for the conducts of the business on the date of occurrence and after obtaining consent from the Joint Directors of the Health Services, Kamrup Guwahati.
texts.arguments: Section 17(2) of the P.F.A. Act 1954 says that any company may, by order in Page No.# 3/5 writing, authorize any of its directors or managers to exercise all such powers and take all such steps as may be necessary or expedient to prevent the Arvind Goel And 3 Ors vs State Of Assam on 28 May, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34670044/ 2 commission by the Company of any offence under this act and may give notice to the Local (Health) Authority. But where no person has been so nominated, every person who at time the offence was committed was in charge of, and was responsible to, the company for the conduct of the business of the company and the company shall be deemed to be guilty of the offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly (Section 17). This has also been held in the reported case of R. Banerjee and Others- Vs- H.D. Dubey and others- (1992) 2 SCC 552. 6. Sub-Section (2) of Section 17 of the Act of 1954 reads as under: "(2) Any company may, by order in writing, authorise any of its directors or managers (such manager being employed mainly in a managerial or supervisory capacity) to exercise all such powers and take all such steps as may be necessary or expedient to prevent the commission by the company of any offence under this Act and may give notice to the Local (Health) Authority, in such form and in such manner as may be prescribed, that it has nominated such director or manager as the person responsible, along with the written consent of such director or manager for being so nominated. Explanation.--Where a company has different establishments or branches or different units in any establishment or branch, different persons may be nominated under this sub-section in relation to different establishments or branches or units and the person nominated in relation to any establishment, branch or unit shall be deemed to be the person responsible in respect of such establishment, branch or unit." 7.
